All 3 tabs (studio-tab-image/text/research) show correct per-op cost, engine-chatgpt/engine-claude toggles work, studio-image-output renders with base64 data URL + download link, studio-text-output renders text, nav-credits chip stays in sync with studio-credits after refreshUser(). Credit-packs section renders Spark $9/120, Pro $19/350 (BEST VALUE), Studio $29/800 (POWER USER); buy-pro redirects to https://checkout.stripe.com showing 'Pro Pack — 350 AI Studio credits — US$19.00'. critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 777 lines (up from 646). Studio endpoints, credit helpers (ensure_credits/require_credits/spend_credits), credit-pack checkout branch, and fulfill_transaction are now all inline. Splitting into routers/studio.py + routers/payments.py + services/credits.py is overdue.

STUDIO_COST is a module-level dict but /studio/credits returns it directly (`return {..., 'costs': STUDIO_COST}`). This means a mutation anywhere in the process would leak. Consider returning `dict(STUDIO_COST)` (shallow copy) for immutability.

spend_credits uses a raw $inc without a `credits: {$gte: cost}` filter, so a race condition between two concurrent generations could drive credits negative even though require_credits gated it. Recommend `update_one({'user_id': u, 'credits': {'$gte': cost}}, {'$inc': {'credits': -cost}})` + inspect modified_count for atomicity.

studio_text/research/image call spend_credits AFTER the AI call succeeds — good for user (no charge on failure) but if the AI succeeds and the DB update fails, the user gets the output free. Low risk but worth wrapping in try/except with a warning log.

fulfill_transaction relies on `is_credit_pack` set in each item at checkout time. If a legacy transaction (pre-iter-4) is replayed via webhook it will not grant credits — acceptable but flag if backfilling is ever needed.

OpenAIImageGeneration import in server.py is used only once (studio_image). Fine, but consider a small retry with exponential backoff on transient 5xx — gpt-image-1 occasionally times out at ~60s and the current 502 message is generic.

The Studio.jsx `run()` sets `setBusy(true); setTextOut(''); setImgOut('');` before the API call, which means on a 402 the previous output is wiped and the user just sees the error toast — minor UX loss (they lose their last generation view). Not critical.
Navbar nav-credits chip uses `user.credits ?? 0` — for a brief tick between login and /auth/me hydration the chip may flash '0'. Consider showing '—' until user object hydrates.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-4 tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py. Uses a module-scoped `fresh_user` fixture (registers via POST /api/auth/register and holds both cookie session + Bearer). 14 tests covering: (a) /studio/credits requires auth + fresh user has 30 credits + correct costs dict, (b) /credit-packs returns exactly Spark/Pro/Studio with correct credits/price/lookup_key, (c) /studio/text with empty prompt -> 400, chatgpt returns engine containing 'GPT' and deducts 2, claude returns engine containing 'Claude' and deducts 2, (d) /studio/research deducts 4, (e) /studio/image deducts 15 and returns base64>1000 chars (uses 120s timeout), (f) 402 enforcement: drain fresh user to 13 credits, attempt 15-credit image -> 402 with balance unchanged, (g) 3 credit-pack Stripe checkouts (credits_spark/pro/studio) all return https://checkout.stripe.com URLs, (h) regression: 65 tools + 4 bundles. Full suite (all 4 iterations) runs in ~46s via `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -v` with 2 xdist workers.
